category_description: Superannuation and the Age Pension in Australia.
subcategory_description: How super works, and the limits on putting money into it.
label: Concessional contributions cap
context: The most that can go into super each year at the concessional rate. It covers employer contributions, salary sacrifice and personal contributions claimed as a tax deduction, across all of a person's funds.

category_description: Superannuation and the Age Pension in Australia.
subcategory_description: How super works, and the limits on putting money into it.
label: Non-concessional contributions cap
context: The most that can go into super each year from after-tax money, such as personal contributions that are not claimed as a deduction. It is counted across all of a person's funds.

category_description: Superannuation and the Age Pension in Australia.
subcategory_description: How super works, and the limits on putting money into it.
label: Total super balance limit for carrying forward unused cap
context: To use unused concessional cap from earlier years, the total super balance must be under this amount on 30 June of the previous financial year.

category_description: Superannuation and the Age Pension in Australia.
subcategory_description: How super works, and the limits on putting money into it.
label: Years unused concessional cap can be carried forward
context: Unused concessional cap can be used for up to 5 years, after which it expires.

category_description: Superannuation and the Age Pension in Australia.
subcategory_description: How super works, and the limits on putting money into it.
label: General transfer balance cap
context: A person whose total super balance is at or above this amount on 30 June cannot make non-concessional contributions in the next financial year without them being excess contributions.
